name: Two pointers (left / right)
whenToUse: The standard answer: n / 2 swaps, in place, no extra array.

card.signals: "reverse" means the first character trades places with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on. "In place with O(1) extra memory" rules out building a reversed copy. Both point to two pointers that start at the ends and swap as they move towards each other.
card.pattern: two pointers, towards each other: left starts at index 0, right at the last index. One swap per round, n / 2 rounds. O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
card.coreIdea: Swap s[left] and s[right], then move both inwards. When they meet or cross, every character is in its reversed place. In an odd-length string the middle character never moves.

invariant: Everything outside [left, right] is already in its final, reversed place. Inside [left, right] nothing has moved yet.

legend.text: left: next character from the front
right: next character from the back
